LinkedIn Secretly Scans 6,000+ Chrome Extensions and Collects Device Data


Apr 3, 20:40


LinkedIn is using hidden JavaScript scripts to scan visitors' browsers for installed extensions and collect device data without user knowledge or consent. The investigation by European advocacy group Fairlinked e.V., dubbed 'BrowserGate,' found the scanning occurs every time users open LinkedIn in Chrome-based browsers. LinkedIn's privacy policy makes no mention of this data collection practice.

Sources: BleepingComputer · Cybersecurity News

Apr 3, 17:34


Chinese threat actor TA416 has resumed targeting European government and diplomatic organizations since mid-2025 after a two-year hiatus from the region. The campaign employs PlugX malware and OAuth-based phishing techniques to compromise diplomatic communications. TA416 overlaps with multiple known threat groups including DarkPeony, RedDelta, and UNC6384.


Nation-state espionage affecting European government diplomatic communications and demonstrating renewed Chinese interest in European intelligence targets


Sources: The Hacker News


CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch Video Conferencing Bug Exploited by Chinese Hackers


Apr 3, 19:45


CISA has given federal agencies two weeks to patch a vulnerability in TrueConf video conferencing software that is being actively exploited by hackers. Chinese threat actors are using the flaw to perform reconnaissance, escalate privileges, and execute additional payloads against government systems. The vulnerability has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Apr 3, 16:36
